atomicity.reason: One obligation (compute the temperature-driven share), with the two saturation regions and the interpolation as parts of one function definition.

comprehensibility.reason: The two endpoints and the interpolation rule are all inline; the reader needs no adjacent requirement to compute the ramp shape.

feasibility.reason: A two-point linear interpolation on a temperature is trivial and consistent with the 35/30 degC cooling band that precedes the derating region.

parent_fit.reason: ARCH_POWER_LIMIT_CALCULATOR owns the temperature-driven limit as a linear ramp from 100 % at 55 degC to 0 % at 60 degC; this requirement states that ramp with both boundaries inclusive.

unambiguity.reason: Behaviour is undefined when the highest cell temperature is unavailable - SWREQ_TEMP_EXTREMA publishes no figures in a cycle with no valid temperature sample - so the share in that case reads either as held or as the fail-safe 0 %.
unambiguity.suggestion: Add the fail-safe case explicitly, e.g. 'when no highest cell temperature is available the temperature-driven share shall be 0 %'.

verifiability.reason: The ramp's endpoints and inclusivity are exact, but the percentage has no stated reference quantity and no update period is given, so neither the absolute expected value nor the required response time is testable.
verifiability.suggestion: State the base the percentage applies to (e.g. '% of the rated discharge power') and the cycle on which the share is recomputed (e.g. once per 100 ms cycle).

summary: The ramp matches the parent exactly; what is missing is the base the percentage refers to, the update rate of a safety-relevant derating, and the fail-safe value when the highest cell temperature is unavailable.
